body: Thanks for spotting that. It must’ve caused while merging commits.

`screenHeight * 0.15` 

What exactly is being calculated here? I've often seen other places where something has been hard-coded, usually not correctly on every display size and resolution.

example: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/83743#issuecomment-2923389966

It’s a workaround to estimate whether the keyboard is visible. If the height difference exceeds 15% of the screen height, we assume the keyboard is being shown.

The 15% threshold is an empirical value, not exact, but chosen because the keyboard typically covers much more than that. It helps avoid false positives caused by minor layout changes or system UI elements like the navigation bar.
I couldn’t find a more reliable solution than this.

I'll try to find time tomorrow to test it thoroughly on different devices. I think we need to read the `density`, which is also necessary for other functions.

- `density`: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/DisplayMetrics#density
- or `densityDpi`: https://developer.android.com/reference/android/util/DisplayMetrics#densityDpi

> It helps avoid false positives caused by minor layout changes or system UI elements like the navigation bar.

Yes, that's true. There are many differences depending on the virtual keyboard app installed (Samsung / Google). I'm trying to do some research on that, too.

I don’t think we need `density` in this case since we're using a percentage of the screen height instead of hardcoded pixel values. This should be consistant accross devices.

> I'll try to find time tomorrow to test it thoroughly on different devices.

Okay!
